name: Martin Hannett
hook: Isolated the drums, gated the reverb, and made a Manchester punk band's aftermath sound like it was recorded in an empty warehouse at 3am.
blurb: Hannett produced Joy Division's two albums, 'Unknown Pleasures' (1979) and 'Closer' (1980), both released by the Manchester label Factory Records, which he was closely tied to. He used techniques that were unusual for the time, separating and gating the drums and layering artificial reverb and echo, to build a sound far starker than the band's live shows. He is often credited with defining Joy Division's recorded sound as much as their own songwriting did. That is genuinely disputed among the surviving members, some of whom have said the records sound more like Hannett's idea than their live sets did at the time.

signatureTracks.title: Unknown Pleasures (produced for Joy Division)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The debut album where Hannett's spacious, gated production first defined the band's recorded identity.

signatureTracks.title: Closer (produced for Joy Division)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Released weeks after Ian Curtis's death, and the fuller realization of Hannett's cold, echo-heavy approach.
